domain_label: System Feedback Loops — Competitor Mechanisms & Faults as a Benchmark Loop
purpose: A method for running the competitor scan (Anki/FSRS, SuperMemo, Quizlet, Duolingo, RemNote, Memrise, Brainscape, and the INBDE/TOEFL exam-prep verticals) as a recurring benchmark feedback loop that feeds the study system's own design: extracting the mechanisms worth copying (model-based spaced repetition, streak-with-slack, confidence self-rating, adaptive within-session difficulty, placement-diagnostic-to-plan, free-content funnel + usage-conditioned guarantee) and the faults to avoid (gamification outrunning learning, ease hell, wall-of-text cards, paywalling the active features, content-supply neglect, onboarding cliffs, raw self-rating scheduling, session mastery without spacing, time-boxed access) into an adopt/adapt/reject ledger — stating feature existence as fact, tagging every claim FACT/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN, and never asserting a user count, price, or pass rate the research did not verify.
assumptions: the survey is of public pages/docs only; direct WebFetch was egress-blocked this session, so every [FACT] means 'stated in WebSearch-retrieved content attributed to the cited URL', official-domain URLs preferred
no user counts, revenue figures, or pass rates are asserted except where a vendor publicly claims one (marked as a vendor claim), and third-party-only prices are labeled ESTIMATE with the basis named

this KB is a benchmark loop, not a market-share or pricing-strategy study; it reasons about which competitor mechanisms and faults change our system's design, not about beating a competitor commercially

feature existence (e.g. Anki has FSRS, Duolingo has streak freezes, Brainscape has 1-5 confidence rating) is treated as fact from vendor docs; exact current prices and tier matrices are ESTIMATE or UNKNOWN where only third-party pages or blocked portals carried them
exclusions: the internal nightly-analysis pipeline mechanics (retention calibration, BKT/Elo re-fit, weakness diagnosis, schedule build) belong to the learner-model and scheduler specialists; this KB only supplies the competitor-benchmark lessons those loops consume
the FSRS DSR formulas, revlog schema and optimizer detail belong to the spaced-repetition specialist; here FSRS is cited only as the model-based-SR exemplar to copy
the gamification implementation (streak UI, calendar fill-bar, league design) belongs to the engagement specialist; here Duolingo streaks/leagues are cited only as a mechanism-and-fault reference
flashcard atomicity/authoring lint belongs to the content-engineering specialist; here wall-of-text cards are cited only as a fault-to-avoid design rule
asserting any fabricated user count, revenue figure, pass rate, or an unverified current price as fact

competency_questions.question: What is the competitor scan as a recurring benchmark feedback loop, and how does its output feed the system's own design and nightly loop?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BENCHMARK_LOOP_CHARTER frames the scan as a periodic loop (not a one-off) whose product is design-decisions (adopt/adapt/reject), names the mechanism-vs-fault split as its two outputs, and states that it feeds the design backlog rather than a commercial comparison

competency_questions.question: How is competitor intelligence kept honest given egress-blocked fetches and no verified user counts, prices, or pass rates?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SOURCING_HONESTY_DISCIPLINE states the WebFetch-blocked / WebSearch-verified caveat, the FACT/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN labeling, official-domain preference, that no user count/revenue/pass rate is asserted except a marked vendor claim, and that third-party-only prices are ESTIMATE

competency_questions.question: Which competitors are surveyed, and what is stated as fact versus estimate or unknown for each?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COMPETITOR_ROSTER_MAP lists Anki/FSRS, SuperMemo, Quizlet, Duolingo, RemNote, Memrise, Brainscape and the INBDE/TOEFL verticals, marks feature existence FACT and prices/tier matrices ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN, and notes vendor claims as such

competency_questions.question: How is a mechanism worth copying extracted from a competitor (mechanism -> best exemplar -> what to copy -> evidence base)?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MECHANISM_EXTRACTION_METHOD gives the four-column extraction (mechanism, best exemplar, what-to-copy, evidence base) and the rule that a mechanism is copied for its function, with its evidence tag carried, not because a named brand is popular

competency_questions.question: What model-based spaced-repetition mechanism should be copied from Anki FSRS, and why is it the highest-value copy?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MODEL_BASED_SR_MECH names the FSRS DSR memory state (difficulty/stability/retrievability), the user-set desired retention (default 0.90, ~0.70-0.99 range), parameters fitted to the learner's own history, and the mean-reverting difficulty that eliminates SM-2 ease hell

competency_questions.question: What streak-with-slack mechanism from Duolingo is worth copying, and how must it be bounded so it certifies learning not showing up?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: STREAK_SLACK_MECH names the daily-completion streak plus pre-purchased freezes (max 2, one auto-consumed per missed day) and Duolingo's cited slack-beats-rigid-rules habit research, and binds the copy to 'completed today's due reviews' not 'opened the app'

competency_questions.question: How should Brainscape's 1-5 confidence rating be adopted without letting raw self-rating become the whole scheduler?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONFIDENCE_RATING_MECH names the 1-5 confidence tap as both a cheap scheduling input and a metacognition prompt, and the RAW_SELF_RATING_FAULT rule that confidence is one input feature calibrated against actual recall, never the whole scheduler (confidence != competence)

competency_questions.question: What adaptive within-session difficulty is worth copying from Quizlet Learn, and what spacing fault must be avoided when copying it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ADAPTIVE_DIFFICULTY_MECH names the round-based re-serving of missed items and its low-friction 'it adapts to me' feel (mechanics ESTIMATE, no official algorithm doc), and SESSION_MASTERY_NO_SPACING_FAULT's rule that every session-mastered item must enter a long-term calendar-spaced queue

competency_questions.question: How should a placement diagnostic seed a personalized plan without recreating an expert-tool onboarding cliff?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PLACEMENT_DIAGNOSTIC_MECH names the ETS TestReady study-plan-from-diagnostic (FACT) and Duolingo placement (ESTIMATE) that seeds a plan and skips known material, and ONBOARDING_CLIFF_FAULT's rule that defaults must be correct out of the box with zero required configuration before the first review

competency_questions.question: What monetization-adjacent mechanisms (free-content funnel, usage-conditioned guarantee, quiz-after-video micro-loop) are worth copying, and which pricing faults must be avoided?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FUNNEL_GUARANTEE_MECH names the Mental-Dental-to-INBDE-Bootcamp free-content funnel, the usage-conditioned pass guarantee (Bootcamp/Magoosh/BestMyTest, FACT), and the quiz-after-every-video micro-loop, and pairs them with the paywall-active-features and time-boxed-access faults to avoid

competency_questions.question: How are documented competitor faults turned into design rules for our system, and what are the highest-priority faults to avoid?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FAULT_EXTRACTION_METHOD gives the fault -> where-documented -> design-rule extraction and names gamification-over-learning, ease hell, wall-of-text cards and content-supply neglect as the flagship faults, each with a design rule and its evidence tag

competency_questions.question: How are the extracted mechanisms and faults turned into an adopt/adapt/reject ledger, and when is the benchmark scan re-run?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ADOPT_ADAPT_REJECT_LEDGER records an adopt/adapt/reject verdict with rationale for each mechanism and fault (no verdict resting on an unlabeled or invented fact), and BENCHMARK_REVISIT_CADENCE states the triggers (competitor pricing/feature change, a new entrant, a fault surfacing in our own metrics) that re-run the scan and refresh the ledger

glossary.definition: The recurring competitor-scan feedback loop this KB defines: periodically survey the SR/study-app and exam-prep field, extract mechanisms worth copying and faults to avoid, and fold the lessons into the system's own design backlog — a loop that improves the system, distinct from a commercial market comparison.

The binding honesty contract on every competitor claim: [FACT] = stated in WebSearch-retrieved content attributed to a cited (preferably official-domain) URL; [ESTIMATE] = only third-party pages or reasoning support it, with the basis named; [UNKNOWN] = not verifiable this session (e.g. a portal-gated price). No user count, revenue, or pass rate is asserted except a marked vendor claim.

The Anki-FSRS mechanism worth copying: each card carries a Difficulty / Stability / Retrievability memory state, review is scheduled when predicted retrievability drops to a user-set desired retention (default 0.90, permitted ~0.70-0.99), and parameters are fitted to the learner's own review history; FSRS difficulty mean-reverts on repeated success, which is what eliminates SM-2 ease hell [FACT, ankiweb/open-spaced-repetition].

The Anki SM-2 fault where the per-card ease factor sinks fast on Again/Hard (-20%/-15%) and recovers only on Easy (+15%), so cards stick at the 130% floor and return far too often; the design rule is to use a mean-reverting (FSRS-style) difficulty so a bad week cannot permanently inflate workload [FACT].

The Duolingo mechanism worth copying: a consecutive-day completion streak softened by pre-purchased Streak Freezes (max 2 equipped, one auto-consumed per missed day), which Duolingo's cited habit research frames as flexibility beating rigid rules for persistence; copy it bound to 'completed today's due reviews', never 'opened the app' [FACT].

Brainscape's mechanism: after each card the learner taps confidence 1-5 and the rating drives relative repetition spacing; worth copying as a cheap input signal AND a metacognition prompt, but fed into a real memory model rather than used raw, because confidence != competence and self-rating is gameable [FACT mechanic; ESTIMATE hybrid recommendation].

The Duolingo-documented fault where streak anxiety, XP-farming and league mechanics optimize the daily-return (engagement) loop far better than the learning loop; the design rule is to gamify retrieval events and retention outcomes, never raw time or XP — the streak certifies showing up, not knowing [FACT critiques; ESTIMATE synthesis].

The Dental-Decks-style fault of packing a full topic summary onto one non-atomic card, the anti-pattern the minimum-information principle exists to fix; the design rule is to enforce atomic cards at authoring time and lint card length — one fact per card [ESTIMATE on the format critique; anti-pattern well established].

The INBDE-Bootcamp/Magoosh/BestMyTest mechanism: a refund tied to measurable usage targets (score threshold, % qbank completed, simulations/lessons taken) that aligns incentives, drives completion and de-risks purchase; all three publish conditioned guarantees, and Bootcamp additionally makes a vendor pass-rate claim that is not independently verified [FACT for the guarantees; vendor claim for the rate].

The synthesis output of the loop: for every extracted mechanism and fault, a recorded verdict — adopt as-is, adapt with a stated modification (e.g. confidence rating fed into the model not used raw), or reject with a reason — each carrying its evidence tag, so no design decision rests on an unlabeled or invented competitor fact.

nodes.definition: Charter the competitor scan as a recurring benchmark feedback loop rather than a one-off survey: periodically the system reviews the spaced-repetition / study-app field (Anki/FSRS, SuperMemo, Quizlet, Duolingo, RemNote, Memrise, Brainscape) and the exam-prep verticals (INBDE Bootcamp, Dental Decks, Mental Dental; ETS TestReady, Magoosh, BestMyTest) and turns what it finds into design decisions for our own system. The loop has exactly two products: a mechanism-extraction table of features worth copying and a fault table of anti-patterns to avoid, both feeding an adopt/adapt/reject ledger on the design backlog. This is a benchmark that improves the system (a loop-that-improves-the-loop), explicitly NOT a market-share or pricing-strategy comparison and NOT a plan to beat a named competitor commercially.

included: the scan as a periodic loop feeding design, not a one-off
the two outputs: mechanisms-to-copy and faults-to-avoid
the framing as a design benchmark, not a commercial comparison
excluded: the per-mechanism and per-fault detail (their own nodes)
the internal nightly pipeline that consumes the lessons

pros.claim: Framing the scan as a recurring loop with two defined outputs keeps competitor study producing design decisions instead of trivia
pros.example: each scan closing with an adopt/adapt/reject verdict per mechanism rather than an unused feature list

cons.claim: A benchmark loop can drift into feature-chasing if it is not disciplined to learning-outcome relevance
cons.example: copying a competitor's flashy league because it exists, not because it improves retention

failure_modes: treating the scan as a one-off instead of a maintained loop
letting the loop become a commercial comparison rather than a design input
acceptance_tests: the charter states the loop is recurring, names the mechanism-table and fault-table outputs, and routes them to the adopt/adapt/reject ledger rather than a market comparison
revisit_triggers: a new competitor or category enters the field
the system's own metrics reveal a gap the current scan did not cover
the design backlog stops consuming the ledger's verdicts

base.update_signal: a new entrant, a metric-revealed gap, or an unused ledger changes the charter

nodes.definition: Fix the honesty discipline every competitor claim in the loop must obey. This session's direct page fetches (WebFetch) were egress-blocked for all external hosts, so each [FACT] means 'stated in WebSearch-retrieved content attributed to the cited URL', with official-domain URLs preferred; [ESTIMATE] means only third-party review/pricing pages or reasoning support it, with the basis named; [UNKNOWN] means not verifiable this session (e.g. a portal-gated price like ETS TestReady's itemized prices or SuperMemo 19's current price). No user count, revenue figure, or pass rate is asserted anywhere except where a vendor publicly claims one, which is marked as a vendor claim (e.g. INBDE Bootcamp's '99% of target-meeting students pass'). Feature existence is FACT from vendor docs; exact current prices and tier matrices are ESTIMATE (third-party-corroborated) or UNKNOWN. This discipline gates every downstream mechanism, fault and ledger verdict.

included: the WebFetch-blocked / WebSearch-verified caveat and the FACT/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN definitions
the no-invented-user-counts/revenue/pass-rates rule and the vendor-claim marking
feature-existence-as-FACT vs prices-as-ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN
excluded: the specific competitor claims themselves (roster and mechanism nodes)
the internal system's own metric honesty

pros.claim: A single labeling contract stops an unverified price or a vendor pass-rate claim from entering a design decision as fact
pros.example: carrying INBDE Bootcamp's pass rate explicitly as a vendor claim rather than as an established outcome

cons.claim: Strict labeling slows the scan and leaves some commercially interesting numbers as UNKNOWN
cons.example: having to leave ETS TestReady itemized pricing UNKNOWN because the portal was gated

failure_modes: asserting a third-party-only price or a vendor pass-rate claim as a verified fact
inventing a user count or enumeration the research did not verify
acceptance_tests: every competitor claim carries a FACT/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN tag, vendor claims are marked as such, and no user count/revenue/pass rate is stated as fact
revisit_triggers: direct-fetch access to a gated vendor page is later obtained
a vendor publishes an independently verifiable metric
a claim's tag is challenged as mislabeled

base.update_signal: gated-page access or a challenged tag changes the labeling of a claim

nodes.definition: Map the surveyed competitor set and what is known about each at what confidence. Spaced-repetition / study apps: Anki (free, open-source, FSRS built in since v23.10; iOS AnkiMobile $24.99 one-time [FACT]); SuperMemo (SM-18/19 lineage, incremental reading since v10 [FACT]); Quizlet (user-generated sets, Learn/Write/Test/Match modes; Learn and Test moved behind the paywall in Aug 2022 [FACT]); Duolingo (gamification reference: streaks, freezes, 10-tier leagues [FACT]); RemNote (notes-first, cards-in-notes, PDF annotation + AI generation [FACT]); Memrise (official courses, 'Learn with Locals' native-speaker video, community courses removed [FACT]); Brainscape (1-5 confidence-based repetition [FACT]). Exam-prep verticals: INBDE Bootcamp (3,000+ case items, video + quiz micro-loop, usage-conditioned pass guarantee [FACT]); Dental Decks (2,700+ static flashcards [FACT]); Mental Dental (free YouTube backbone [FACT]); ETS TestReady, Magoosh, BestMyTest for TOEFL [FACT existence]. Feature existence is FACT; prices/tier matrices are ESTIMATE (third-party) or UNKNOWN (portal-gated).

included: the full surveyed roster across SR apps, the gamification reference and the exam-prep verticals
the FACT status of feature existence per competitor
the ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN status of prices and tier matrices
excluded: the mechanism-by-mechanism copy analysis (mechanism nodes)
the fault-by-fault design rules (fault nodes)

pros.claim: A single roster with per-competitor confidence keeps the extraction anchored to real, cited products rather than an idealized composite
pros.example: attributing model-based SR specifically to Anki FSRS and confidence rating specifically to Brainscape

cons.claim: A roster snapshot dates quickly as competitors change pricing and features
cons.example: Quizlet's tier matrix or Duolingo's Max pricing shifting after the scan date

failure_modes: blending distinct competitors into a vague composite that loses the exemplar attribution
letting a stale roster snapshot drive a current design decision
acceptance_tests: the roster names each surveyed competitor, marks feature existence FACT and prices ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN, and preserves the exemplar attribution for each mechanism
revisit_triggers: a competitor changes pricing, tiers, or a flagship feature
a new competitor enters the surveyed field
a previously UNKNOWN price becomes verifiable

base.update_signal: a competitor feature/price change or a new entrant updates the roster

nodes.definition: Define the method for extracting a mechanism worth copying, the four-column discipline behind the 'worth copying' table: (mechanism) name the function abstractly; (best exemplar) attribute it to the competitor that does it best; (what to copy) state the specific portion to lift and the modification if any; (evidence base) carry the FACT/ESTIMATE tag. A mechanism is copied for its function and its evidence, never because a named brand is popular. The ten extracted rows are model-based spaced repetition (Anki FSRS), streak-with-slack (Duolingo), confidence self-rating (Brainscape), adaptive within-session difficulty (Quizlet Learn), placement-diagnostic-to-plan (ETS TestReady / Duolingo), usage-conditioned pass guarantee (Bootcamp/Magoosh/BestMyTest), free-content funnel (Mental Dental -> INBDE Bootcamp), quiz-after-every-video micro-loop (Bootcamp), native-speaker micro-video as card material (Memrise 'Learn with Locals'), and notes<->cards single source of truth (RemNote); this KB deep-models the first six and carries the last three as cited candidates.

included: the mechanism/exemplar/what-to-copy/evidence four-column method
the copy-for-function-not-brand rule
the enumerated ten mechanism rows and which are deep-modeled here
excluded: the internal implementation of each copied mechanism (owning specialist)
the fault-avoidance extraction (its own node)

pros.claim: A fixed four-column method makes every copy decision auditable back to an exemplar and an evidence tag
pros.example: recording 'confidence rating | Brainscape | copy the 1-5 tap but feed a memory model | FACT mechanic, ESTIMATE hybrid'

cons.claim: Abstracting a mechanism from one exemplar can miss context that made it work only in that product
cons.example: copying Quizlet's within-session adaptivity without noting it lacks calendar spacing

failure_modes: copying a mechanism because a brand is popular rather than for its function and evidence
lifting a mechanism without recording the modification needed to fit our system
acceptance_tests: each extracted mechanism has a named function, a best exemplar, a specific what-to-copy with modification, and an evidence tag
revisit_triggers: a competitor ships a new mechanism worth extracting
an extracted mechanism's evidence tag is downgraded
a deep-model reveals a copy needs a different modification

base.update_signal: a new mechanism, a tag downgrade, or a copy-modification change updates the method

nodes.definition: Extract model-based spaced repetition from Anki FSRS as the highest-value copy. FSRS (built into Anki since v23.10) models each card as a three-component memory state — Difficulty, Stability (days for retrievability to fall 100%->90%), Retrievability — and schedules the next review when predicted retrievability drops to a user-chosen desired retention (default 90%, permitted range ~0.70-0.99); parameters are optimized per-preset from the user's own review history [FACT, docs.ankiweb.net + open-spaced-repetition]. Crucially, FSRS difficulty mean-reverts toward baseline on repeated correct answers, which is exactly what eliminates SM-2's ease hell [FACT, expertium algorithm writeup via search]. What to copy: the per-item DSR memory state, the user-set desired-retention dial, history-fitted parameters, and mean-reverting difficulty. This is the scheduler our system already commits to (see the spaced-repetition specialist); the loop's role is to confirm FSRS-class model-based SR as the adopt-as-is baseline against which every other scheduling idea is judged.

included: the FSRS DSR memory state and desired-retention dial (default 0.90, ~0.70-0.99)
history-fitted parameters and mean-reverting difficulty as the ease-hell cure
the adopt-as-is baseline role for scheduling
excluded: the DSR formulas, revlog schema and optimizer detail (SR specialist)
the confidence-rating and adaptive-difficulty mechanisms (their own nodes)

pros.claim: Adopting FSRS-class model-based SR gives a world-class scheduler with a mean-reverting difficulty that structurally avoids ease hell
pros.example: scheduling at a user-set 0.90 desired retention with parameters fitted to the learner's own revlog

cons.claim: Model-based SR needs enough review history to fit parameters, so early behavior leans on defaults
cons.example: a brand-new learner scheduled on default FSRS parameters until their revlog is large enough to optimize

failure_modes: shipping a legacy SM-2 ease-factor scheduler and inheriting ease hell
exposing the desired-retention dial without a sane default and range
acceptance_tests: the copy names the DSR memory state, the desired-retention default 0.90 and ~0.70-0.99 range, history-fitted parameters, and mean-reverting difficulty as the ease-hell cure
revisit_triggers: FSRS ships a new version or parameter set
a scheduling alternative outperforms FSRS-class SR in our metrics
the desired-retention default is retuned

base.update_signal: a new FSRS version, an outperforming alternative, or a default retune changes the baseline

nodes.definition: Extract Duolingo's streak-with-slack as the retention mechanic to copy, bounded to learning. A streak is consecutive days with >=1 completed unit before local midnight; it resets to 0 on a missed day unless a Streak Freeze (bought in advance, max 2 equipped, one auto-consumed per missed day) covers it, and Duolingo's own blog frames this as habit research where flexibility/'slack' beats rigid rules for goal persistence [FACT, blog.duolingo.com]. What to copy: the daily-completion streak plus the pre-purchased freeze slack. The binding modification (from the gamification fault): the streak must certify 'completed today's due reviews', never 'opened the app' — it is the single most-copied retention mechanic in edtech and is content-agnostic, certifying showing up, not knowing, unless it is tied to retrieval events [ESTIMATE synthesis]. The freeze slack is the piece that reduces streak anxiety while keeping the habit.

included: the daily-completion streak and the pre-purchased freeze (max 2, one per missed day)
the slack-beats-rigid-rules habit rationale
the modification binding the streak to due-reviews-completed not app-opened
excluded: the streak/calendar UI and league design (engagement specialist)
the gamification-over-learning fault rule itself (its own node)

pros.claim: A freeze-softened daily streak captures the strongest documented habit mechanic while the slack cuts streak anxiety
pros.example: a two-freeze buffer that lets a learner miss a day without losing a long streak

cons.claim: The streak is content-agnostic, so copied naively it rewards attendance rather than learning
cons.example: a streak that increments on any app-open, encouraging empty check-ins

failure_modes: incrementing the streak on app-open rather than on completed due reviews
omitting the freeze slack and manufacturing streak anxiety
acceptance_tests: the copy names the daily streak, the pre-purchased freeze (max 2, one per missed day), the slack rationale, and binds the streak to completed due reviews
revisit_triggers: Duolingo changes its streak or freeze mechanics
our own metrics show streak anxiety or empty check-ins
the streak-to-retrieval binding is redefined

base.update_signal: a Duolingo mechanic change or a streak-anxiety signal updates the copy

nodes.definition: Extract Brainscape's 1-5 confidence rating as an input feature and metacognition prompt. In Brainscape's Confidence-Based Repetition, after each card the learner rates confidence 1-5 ('not at all' -> 'totally confident') and the rating drives relative repetition spacing — low confidence returns soon, high confidence is pushed far out; intervals are relative within the study stream so a deck of all-5s still cycles, letting users re-rate honestly [FACT, brainscape help center]. What to copy: the cheap 1-5 tap, which doubles as a metacognition prompt with its own learning value. The binding modification (from the raw-self-rating fault): feed the confidence signal into a real memory model calibrated against actual recall, never use it raw as the whole scheduler, because confidence != competence and 5 buckets are coarser than a forgetting-curve model (overconfident novices under-schedule). The virtue to keep is the metacognition prompt; the fault to avoid is letting the tap be the scheduler.

included: the 1-5 confidence tap as input and metacognition prompt
the relative-repetition detail that keeps re-rating honest
the modification feeding confidence into a calibrated model not using it raw
excluded: the memory model that consumes the signal (learner-model / SR specialists)
the raw-self-rating fault rule itself (its own node)

pros.claim: A 1-5 confidence tap is a near-free input that also prompts metacognition, which itself aids learning
pros.example: capturing self-rated confidence per card as a feature alongside actual correctness

cons.claim: Self-rating is subjective and gameable, and 5 buckets are coarse versus a forgetting-curve model
cons.example: an overconfident novice rating 5 and under-scheduling a card they will soon forget

failure_modes: using the raw confidence rating as the whole scheduler
ignoring the metacognition value and discarding the signal entirely
acceptance_tests: the copy names the 1-5 tap as input and metacognition prompt and requires feeding it into a recall-calibrated model rather than using it raw
revisit_triggers: calibration shows self-rating diverges badly from actual recall
Brainscape changes its confidence scale
the confidence feature's weight in the model is retuned

base.update_signal: a calibration divergence or a scale change updates the confidence copy

nodes.definition: Extract Quizlet Learn's within-session adaptivity as the low-friction 'it adapts to me' feel, with the spacing caveat attached. Quizlet Learn is mastery/round-based: it focuses on missed items and moves through rounds, re-serving missed items until answered correctly — adaptive within a session but not calendar spaced repetition [ESTIMATE, medium-high; Quizlet markets adaptivity but publishes no interval algorithm, no official algorithm doc found]. What to copy: the round-based re-serving of missed items and the immediate low-friction adaptation feel that makes a session feel responsive. The binding modification (from the session-mastery fault): within-session mastery must NOT be the end state — every item Quizlet would call 'mastered' has to enter our long-term, calendar-spaced FSRS queue, because session mastery without spacing decays between cram sessions. Copy the in-session feel; reject the missing long-term scheduler.

included: the round-based missed-item re-serving and the low-friction adaptation feel
the ESTIMATE status of the mechanics (no official algorithm doc)
the modification routing session-mastered items into the long-term spaced queue
excluded: the model-based SR scheduler that owns long-term spacing (its own node)
the session-mastery fault rule itself (its own node)

pros.claim: Round-based missed-item recycling gives a responsive in-session feel that raises engagement cheaply
pros.example: re-serving the items a learner missed this session until they get them right before ending the round

cons.claim: Session-only mastery decays between sessions because it has no calendar-spaced follow-up
cons.example: a learner 'mastering' a set in one Quizlet Learn session and forgetting it a week later

failure_modes: treating within-session mastery as the end state with no long-term queue
over-claiming Quizlet's adaptivity as a known algorithm when its mechanics are ESTIMATE
acceptance_tests: the copy names the round-based re-serving as ESTIMATE mechanics and requires every session-mastered item to enter the long-term calendar-spaced queue
revisit_triggers: Quizlet publishes or changes its Learn algorithm
our in-session-to-long-term handoff shows leakage
a better within-session adaptivity exemplar appears

base.update_signal: a published Learn algorithm or a handoff-leakage signal updates the copy

nodes.definition: Extract the placement-diagnostic-to-plan mechanism that seeds a personalized study plan and skips known material. ETS TOEFL TestReady's free tier generates a survey-based personalized study plan with progress tracking [FACT, ets.org], and Duolingo offers a placement test that starts a learner mid-path rather than at zero [ESTIMATE]. What to copy: a short diagnostic that seeds a plan and skips material the learner already knows, so the first sessions are neither trivial nor overwhelming. The binding modification (from the onboarding-cliff fault): the diagnostic must not become a configuration cliff — defaults must be correct out of the box with zero required configuration before the first review, unlike the expert-tool onboarding of SuperMemo/Anki/RemNote. Copy the seed-a-plan-from-a-short-diagnostic idea; keep the first-review path free of mandatory setup.

included: the short-diagnostic-seeds-a-plan-and-skips-known-material mechanism
the TestReady FACT and Duolingo-placement ESTIMATE attributions
the modification keeping the first-review path free of mandatory configuration
excluded: the learner-model that estimates initial mastery (learner specialist)
the onboarding-cliff fault rule itself (its own node)

pros.claim: A short diagnostic that seeds a plan and skips known material makes the first sessions well-targeted without heavy setup
pros.example: a placement check that starts a learner at their level instead of at zero

cons.claim: A diagnostic that grows into a long mandatory setup becomes the very onboarding cliff it should avoid
cons.example: forcing extensive configuration before the learner can do a single review

failure_modes: turning the diagnostic into a mandatory configuration cliff before the first review
over-claiming Duolingo placement as FACT when it is ESTIMATE
acceptance_tests: the copy names the diagnostic-seeds-a-plan mechanism with correct FACT/ESTIMATE tags and requires zero mandatory configuration before the first review
revisit_triggers: TestReady or Duolingo changes its placement/plan flow
onboarding metrics show drop-off before the first review
the diagnostic length is retuned

nodes.definition: Extract the monetization-adjacent mechanisms that align commercial and learning incentives. Free-content funnel: Mental Dental's free authoritative YouTube videos build trust and feed the paid INBDE Bootcamp layer (which licenses the same instructor's videos) — a proven free-content-into-paid-structured-practice model [FACT, the relationship is public]. Usage-conditioned pass guarantee: INBDE Bootcamp, Magoosh and BestMyTest publish refunds tied to measurable usage targets (score threshold, % qbank completed, simulations/lessons taken), which aligns incentives, drives completion and de-risks purchase [FACT for the guarantees]; Bootcamp additionally claims 99% of target-meeting students pass — a vendor claim, not independently verified. Quiz-after-every-video micro-loop: Bootcamp puts a bite-sized quiz immediately after each passive video, converting watching into retrieval [FACT]. What to copy: the free-trust funnel, the usage-conditioned guarantee structure, and the quiz-after-content retrieval micro-loop — with the binding modifications from the paywall and time-boxed faults.

the vendor-claim marking on Bootcamp's pass rate
the pointer to the paywall and time-boxed faults as the binding modifications
excluded: the pricing-tier design and monetization strategy (out of scope)
the paywall and time-boxed fault rules themselves (their own nodes)

pros.claim: A free-trust funnel plus a usage-conditioned guarantee and a retrieval micro-loop align commercial and learning incentives at once
pros.example: free videos building trust, a completion-tied refund driving usage, and a post-video quiz converting watching into recall

cons.claim: Guarantee conditions can effectively demand near-total completion, and the model can tempt paywalling the active features
cons.example: a score-improvement guarantee that requires finishing nearly the whole course to qualify

failure_modes: asserting Bootcamp's pass rate as fact rather than a vendor claim
copying the funnel while paywalling the core retention loop
acceptance_tests: the copy names the free funnel, the usage-conditioned guarantee (with the pass rate marked a vendor claim), and the quiz-after-video micro-loop, and points to the paywall/time-boxed faults as modifications

nodes.definition: Define the method for extracting a fault to avoid, the discipline behind the 'faults to avoid' table: (fault) name the anti-pattern; (where documented) attribute it to the competitor(s) where it is evidenced with its FACT/ESTIMATE tag; (design rule) state the enforceable rule it produces for our system. A fault only earns a design rule if it is documented (cited critique or acknowledged vendor limitation), not merely suspected. The extracted faults are gamification-outrunning-learning (Duolingo), ease hell (Anki SM-2), wall-of-text/non-atomic cards (Dental Decks), paywalling the active features while free keeps passive ones (Quizlet 2022), removing/abandoning community content and unvetted shared marketplaces (Memrise, Quizlet Gravity, Anki shared decks), expert-tool onboarding cliff (SuperMemo/Anki/RemNote), raw self-rating as the whole scheduler (Brainscape), session mastery without calendar spacing (Quizlet Learn), and time-boxed access punishing slow studiers (Bootcamp/Dental Decks windows). Each becomes a rule the design backlog must honor.

the documented-not-suspected requirement with evidence tags
the enumerated fault list and its design-rule outputs
excluded: the internal enforcement of each design rule (owning specialist)

cons.claim: Requiring documentation means a real but undocumented fault is not yet turned into a rule

failure_modes: turning a merely-suspected weakness into a rule without documentation
producing a fault observation with no enforceable design rule attached
acceptance_tests: each extracted fault has a named anti-pattern, a documented source with an evidence tag, and an enforceable design rule

nodes.definition: Avoid gamification outrunning learning, the flagship Duolingo-documented fault: widely published critiques flag streak anxiety and compulsive use, leaderboards that reward XP-farming over learning, and 'false fluency' — completing a course without conversational ability [FACT critiques]. The mechanics optimize the engagement loop (daily return) superbly and the learning loop only weakly; the streak is the single most-copied retention mechanic in edtech and is content-agnostic, certifying showing up, not knowing [ESTIMATE synthesis]. Design rule: gamify retrieval events and retention outcomes, never raw time or XP — the streak counts 'completed today's due reviews', progress meters track predicted retention and mastery, and no engagement metric is ever a proxy for knowledge. This is the modification that makes the streak-with-slack mechanism safe to adopt.

included: the streak-anxiety / XP-farming / false-fluency critiques
the engagement-loop-vs-learning-loop framing
the design rule to gamify retrieval and retention, never raw time/XP
excluded: the streak/league UI implementation (engagement specialist)
the streak-with-slack mechanism copy itself (its own node)

pros.claim: Binding all gamification to retrieval and retention outcomes keeps engagement mechanics from faking learning
pros.example: a streak that only advances when the day's due reviews are actually completed

cons.claim: Outcome-bound gamification is less immediately addictive than raw XP/streak farming
cons.example: a learner who cannot pad a streak by trivial app-opens may engage less on a hard day

failure_modes: using an engagement metric (XP, time, app-opens) as a proxy for knowledge
shipping leaderboards that reward farming over retention
acceptance_tests: the rule requires every gamified signal to track a retrieval event or retention outcome and forbids raw time/XP as a knowledge proxy
revisit_triggers: engagement metrics rise while retention stalls (farming signature)

the streak-to-retrieval binding is redefined

base.update_signal: a farming signature or a new gamification critique updates the rule

nodes.definition: Avoid ease hell, the Anki SM-2 fault where the per-card ease factor sinks fast on Again (-20%) and Hard (-15%) and recovers only on Easy (+15%), so cards get stuck at the 130% floor and return far too often [FACT, community docs]. The punitive, hard-to-recover difficulty state means a run of bad answers permanently inflates a card's workload. Design rule: use a mean-reverting (FSRS-style) difficulty so a bad week must not permanently inflate workload — difficulty drifts back toward baseline on repeated success rather than ratcheting down. This fault is precisely what the model-based-SR mechanism cures; the loop records it as the reason the FSRS-class scheduler is adopt-as-is and a legacy SM-2 ease-factor scheduler is rejected.

included: the SM-2 ease-factor sink/recover asymmetry and 130% floor
the punitive permanent-workload-inflation harm
the mean-reverting-difficulty design rule
excluded: the FSRS DSR formula detail (SR specialist)
the model-based-SR mechanism copy itself (its own node)

pros.claim: Requiring mean-reverting difficulty structurally prevents a bad week from permanently inflating a card's return frequency
pros.example: a card's difficulty drifting back to baseline after a recovery streak rather than staying pinned at the floor

cons.claim: Mean-reverting difficulty forgives struggle that in rare cases signals a genuinely hard card needing more repetition
cons.example: a truly hard card whose difficulty reverts before the learner has actually secured it

failure_modes: adopting a legacy SM-2 ease-factor scheduler and inheriting ease hell
letting difficulty ratchet down without a reversion path
acceptance_tests: the rule names the SM-2 sink/recover asymmetry and mandates a mean-reverting difficulty so a bad week cannot permanently inflate workload
revisit_triggers: workload analysis shows cards pinned at a difficulty floor
a scheduler change reintroduces a non-reverting difficulty
the reversion behavior is retuned

base.update_signal: a pinned-difficulty signal or a scheduler change updates the rule

nodes.definition: Avoid wall-of-text / non-atomic cards, the Dental-Decks-style fault where board-prep cards traditionally pack a full topic summary onto one card — the anti-pattern the minimum-information principle exists to fix [ESTIMATE on the format critique; anti-pattern well established, based on product format and long-standing prep-community characterization, not a fetched card sample]. A dense card mixes many facts, so a single lapse cannot localize what was forgotten and scheduling is muddied. Design rule: enforce atomic cards at authoring time and lint card length — one fact per card. This is the design constraint the flashcard-quality specialist enforces; the loop records it as a hard authoring rule so our content does not inherit the static-deck-of-summaries fault, and pairs it with the reminder that Dental Decks also lacks an adaptive scheduler.

included: the wall-of-text / non-atomic card anti-pattern and its ESTIMATE tag
the localization/scheduling harm of multi-fact cards
the atomic-card / lint-length / one-fact-per-card design rule
excluded: the authoring-lint implementation (content-engineering specialist)
the adaptive-scheduler absence detail (roster/other faults)

pros.claim: Enforcing atomic cards at authoring time makes lapses localizable and scheduling clean
pros.example: splitting a topic-summary card into single-fact cards so a lapse points to exactly one fact

cons.claim: Strict atomicity can multiply card count and fragment a concept that benefits from being seen whole
cons.example: over-splitting a tightly linked definition into fragments that lose the connective context

failure_modes: authoring topic-summary cards that pack many facts onto one card
shipping a static deck of summaries with no length lint
acceptance_tests: the rule names the wall-of-text anti-pattern (ESTIMATE) and mandates atomic cards with a card-length lint at authoring time
revisit_triggers: a card sample is fetched that confirms or revises the format critique
lapse analysis shows non-localizable multi-fact cards
the atomicity lint threshold is retuned

base.update_signal: a fetched card sample or a non-localizable-lapse signal updates the rule

nodes.definition: Avoid paywalling the active (effective) features while the free tier keeps only passive ones, the Quizlet-2022 fault: in August 2022 Quizlet moved Learn and Test modes behind the paywall (free users left with ~5 Learn rounds and 1 practice test per set), producing sustained student backlash ('predatory... preys on broke students'), and critics note the free features left are the passive ones (flip cards, match) while the evidence-based active-recall features are paid [FACT]. Design rule: keep the core retention loop (spaced review, active recall) free or cheap and monetize content depth, feedback and analytics instead — never gate the mechanism that actually produces learning. This is the modification that makes the free-content-funnel and usage-guarantee mechanisms safe to adopt: the funnel may monetize depth, but not the active-recall core.

included: the Quizlet-2022 move of Learn/Test behind the paywall and the backlash
the passive-free / active-paid inversion critique
the design rule keeping the active-recall core free and monetizing depth/feedback/analytics
excluded: the pricing-tier design itself (out of scope)
the funnel/guarantee mechanism copy (its own node)

pros.example: monetizing extra content and analytics while spaced review and active recall stay free

cons.claim: Leaving the most valuable loop free narrows the paid surface and pressures monetizing depth harder
cons.example: having to build strong paid analytics/content because the core loop cannot be gated

leaving only passive features (flip, match) in the free tier

a competitor's paywall change resets the norm

base.update_signal: a core-gating proposal or a free-tier retention drop updates the rule

nodes.definition: Avoid content-supply neglect, a paired fault documented across several competitors: (a) removing or abandoning community content — Memrise moved community/user-generated courses off to a separate archive, sharply reducing available content, and Quizlet removed the Gravity game entirely [FACT], both read by users as trust-destroying; and (b) an unvetted shared-content marketplace with no quality signal — Anki's shared decks are unvetted with no accuracy/completeness signal, which is the biggest content-model weakness when the scheduler is world-class but the content supply chain is unmanaged [FACT existence; ESTIMATE on severity]. Design rules: if user-generated content is accepted, treat it as a durable commitment (version and export it, never silently remove it); and curate or score shared decks with provenance and accuracy signals. The loop records content supply as a first-class design surface, not an afterthought behind the scheduler.

included: the Memrise community-removal and Quizlet-Gravity-removal trust faults
the Anki unvetted-shared-deck no-quality-signal fault
the durable-commitment and curate/score-with-provenance design rules
excluded: the content-authoring pipeline itself (content-engineering specialist)
the paywall fault (its own node)

pros.claim: Treating community content as a durable, versioned commitment and scoring shared decks protects trust and content quality
pros.example: versioning and exporting user decks and attaching provenance/accuracy signals rather than silently removing content

cons.claim: Durable content commitments and curation add maintenance and moderation cost
cons.example: having to preserve and export every user deck and score shared content for accuracy indefinitely

failure_modes: silently removing or abandoning accepted user-generated content
shipping an unvetted shared-deck marketplace with no quality or provenance signal
acceptance_tests: the rule treats accepted user content as a versioned, exportable commitment and requires provenance/accuracy signals on shared decks
revisit_triggers: a decision to remove or archive user content is proposed

a competitor content-removal event resets user expectations

base.update_signal: a content-removal proposal or a shared-deck accuracy complaint updates the rule

nodes.definition: Avoid the expert-tool onboarding cliff documented across SuperMemo, Anki and RemNote: SuperMemo's own vendor acknowledges it is 'optimized to make a life of a pro easy... makes life of beginners hard' and is Windows-only with a dated, cluttered UI; Anki has a steep learning curve and defaults widely considered poor, historically requiring add-ons and tutorials; RemNote reviews cite a steep learning curve and time spent structuring notes instead of studying [FACT]. The net lesson (SuperMemo): the most sophisticated algorithm plus incremental reading achieves near-zero adoption outside enthusiasts because onboarding cost is extreme [ESTIMATE]. Design rule: defaults must be correct out of the box with zero required configuration before the first review — the learner reaches a real review in seconds, not after tuning presets. This is the modification that makes the placement-diagnostic mechanism safe: a diagnostic may seed a plan but must never become mandatory setup.

included: the SuperMemo/Anki/RemNote steep-curve and poor-default evidence
the near-zero-adoption-from-onboarding-cost lesson
the zero-config-before-first-review design rule
excluded: the placement-diagnostic mechanism copy (its own node)
the notes-tinkering-substitutes-for-retrieval detail beyond onboarding

pros.claim: Requiring correct out-of-the-box defaults gets a learner to a real review immediately and avoids the adoption-killing cliff
pros.example: a first review reachable in seconds with no preset tuning, unlike the expert-tool onboarding

cons.claim: Zero-config defaults must be good enough for everyone, constraining how much early personalization is exposed
cons.example: hiding advanced scheduler knobs that a power user might want on day one

failure_modes: requiring configuration or add-ons before the first review
exposing expert knobs that turn onboarding into a tuning exercise
acceptance_tests: the rule mandates correct defaults out of the box and zero required configuration before the learner's first review
revisit_triggers: onboarding metrics show drop-off before the first review

base.update_signal: an onboarding drop-off or a wrong-default finding updates the rule

nodes.definition: Avoid raw self-rating as the whole scheduler, the Brainscape fault: Confidence-Based Repetition drives spacing purely from a 1-5 confidence tap, and the obvious objection — self-rating is subjective and gameable — is acknowledged in Brainscape's own help center, answered with a 'relative repetition' argument [FACT mechanic]. But CBR with 5 buckets is coarser than model-based scheduling (no forgetting curve, no per-item difficulty model), and confidence != competence: metacognitive miscalibration is a known failure mode where overconfident novices under-schedule [ESTIMATE weakness]. Design rule: use confidence as ONE input feature, calibrated against actual recall performance, never as the whole scheduler. This is the exact modification the confidence-rating mechanism carries — keep the metacognition-prompt virtue, discard the raw-scheduler role — and it is why a forgetting-curve model owns the final scheduling decision.

included: the Brainscape raw-self-rating-as-scheduler fault and its acknowledged gameability
the coarse-5-buckets and confidence!=competence weakness
the design rule using confidence as one recall-calibrated input feature
excluded: the memory model that owns scheduling (SR/learner specialists)
the confidence-rating mechanism copy itself (its own node)

pros.claim: Demoting confidence to one calibrated input keeps its metacognition value while a forgetting-curve model owns scheduling
pros.example: weighting a self-rated 5 down when that learner's actual recall history contradicts it

cons.claim: Calibrating self-rating against recall needs enough history, so early on the confidence signal is weakly trusted
cons.example: a new learner whose confidence taps cannot yet be calibrated against a recall record

failure_modes: letting the raw confidence tap drive scheduling with no recall calibration
trusting an overconfident novice's high ratings and under-scheduling
acceptance_tests: the rule uses confidence as one input feature calibrated against actual recall and forbids it as the whole scheduler
revisit_triggers: calibration shows systematic self-rating miscalibration
the confidence feature weight is retuned
Brainscape changes its CBR argument or scale

base.update_signal: a self-rating miscalibration or a feature-weight retune updates the rule

nodes.definition: Avoid session mastery without calendar spacing, the Quizlet-Learn structural fault: 'mastery' is per-session (round-based, focused on missed items within the session) with no true long-term scheduler, so retention decays between cram sessions [ESTIMATE]. A learner can finish a Learn session feeling they have mastered a set and forget most of it within days because nothing schedules a spaced follow-up. Design rule: every item a session would call 'mastered' must enter the long-term, calendar-spaced (FSRS-class) review queue — session mastery is a within-session milestone, not an exit condition. This is the modification that makes the adaptive-within-session-difficulty mechanism safe to copy: keep the responsive in-session feel, but hand every mastered item to the memory model so it is spaced over the calendar, not abandoned at session end.

included: the Quizlet-Learn per-session-mastery-without-spacing fault (ESTIMATE)
the between-session decay harm
the design rule routing every session-mastered item into the long-term spaced queue
excluded: the long-term SR scheduler mechanics (SR specialist)
the adaptive-difficulty mechanism copy itself (its own node)

pros.claim: Routing every session-mastered item into the spaced queue prevents the between-session decay of cram-style mastery
pros.example: handing a set 'mastered' in one session to the FSRS queue so it is reviewed on a spaced calendar

cons.claim: Forcing every mastered item into the long-term queue adds scheduled review load that must be budgeted
cons.example: a session that masters many items generating a heavier spaced-review load the next day

failure_modes: treating within-session mastery as the exit condition with no spaced follow-up
letting session-mastered items skip the long-term queue
acceptance_tests: the rule requires every session-mastered item to enter the long-term calendar-spaced review queue and forbids session mastery as an exit condition
revisit_triggers: between-session retention drops for session-mastered items
the session-to-queue handoff shows leakage
review-load budgeting from mastery is retuned

base.update_signal: a between-session retention drop or a handoff leakage updates the rule

nodes.definition: Avoid time-boxed access punishing slow studiers, the exam-prep-vertical fault: INBDE Bootcamp and Dental Decks sell time-boxed subscription windows (Bootcamp ~1/3/6-month tiers; Dental Decks ~6/12-month), and the subscription clock pressures slow or part-time studiers — notably foreign-trained dentists studying part-time — whose access can expire before they finish [FACT pricing structure; ESTIMATE harm]. Design rule: long-horizon learners need pause/extend options so access is not lost to a countdown clock, and the retention loop must not be structured so that lapsed access erases progress. This is the modification attached to the usage-conditioned-guarantee mechanism: a completion-tied guarantee is good, but it must not combine with a hard time box that punishes exactly the slow learners it should serve.

the foreign-trained-part-time-learner example

excluded: the pricing-tier design itself (out of scope)

erasing progress when access lapses

nodes.definition: Compose the loop's synthesis output: an adopt/adapt/reject ledger recording, for every extracted mechanism and fault, a verdict with rationale and evidence tag. Adopt-as-is: model-based spaced repetition (FSRS DSR) as the scheduling baseline. Adapt-with-modification: streak-with-slack (bind to completed due reviews, not app-opens); confidence rating (feed a recall-calibrated model, not raw); adaptive within-session difficulty (route every mastered item into the long-term spaced queue); placement diagnostic (seed a plan but zero mandatory config); free-content funnel + usage guarantee (never paywall the active-recall core, never hard time-box slow learners). Reject: legacy SM-2 ease-factor scheduling (ease hell), engagement metrics as knowledge proxies, wall-of-text cards, silent removal of user content, unvetted shared decks. No verdict may rest on an unlabeled or invented competitor fact — each carries its FACT/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN tag — and each verdict lands on the design backlog as an actionable item.

nodes.definition: Set the cadence that keeps the benchmark loop alive: define the triggers that re-run the competitor scan and refresh the ledger. Scheduled: a periodic re-scan (competitor pricing and features drift fast — Quizlet's paywall move, Duolingo's Max tier, Memrise's community removal all post-dated earlier expectations), so the roster snapshot is re-verified on a cadence and stale ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN prices are re-checked. Event-driven: a competitor changes a flagship feature or price; a new competitor enters the SR/study-app or exam-prep field; or — the loop-that-improves-the-loop path — one of our own system's feedback metrics surfaces a fault the current ledger already warned about (e.g. engagement rising while retention stalls = the gamification fault materializing), which re-opens the relevant verdict. Each trigger re-runs the mechanism and fault extraction under the same honesty discipline and updates the adopt/adapt/reject ledger; a verdict is never treated as permanent.

conflict_axes.name: engagement_loop_vs_learning_loop
conflict_axes.description: The streak/league engagement mechanics optimize daily return superbly but certify showing up, not knowing, pulling against the learning outcome.
poles: gate gamification to retrieval and retention
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: adopt streak-with-slack but bind every gamified signal to completed due reviews and retention outcomes, never raw time/XP

conflict_axes.name: self_rating_signal_vs_model_scheduling
conflict_axes.description: A 1-5 confidence tap is a cheap, useful signal and metacognition prompt but is subjective, gameable and coarser than a forgetting-curve model.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep confidence as one calibrated input feature and metacognition prompt; let a forgetting-curve model own scheduling

conflict_axes.name: session_mastery_vs_long_term_spacing
conflict_axes.description: Within-session adaptivity feels responsive and satisfying but decays between sessions without a calendar-spaced follow-up.
poles: treat session mastery as the exit condition
route every mastered item into the spaced queue
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep the in-session missed-item recycling for feel but hand every mastered item to the long-term FSRS queue

conflict_axes.name: monetize_depth_vs_paywall_the_core
conflict_axes.description: A monetization funnel needs a paid surface, tempting the gating of the active-recall features that actually produce learning.
poles: keep the active-recall core free and monetize depth
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: monetize content depth, feedback and analytics; keep spaced review and active recall free or cheap

conflict_axes.name: personalized_seed_vs_zero_config_start
conflict_axes.description: A placement diagnostic personalizes the start but can grow into a mandatory-setup onboarding cliff that kills adoption.
poles: reach a real review with zero mandatory config
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: let a short diagnostic seed a plan and skip known material, but require correct defaults and zero mandatory config before the first review

conflict_axes.name: completion_pressure_vs_slow_learner_access
conflict_axes.description: A usage-conditioned guarantee and subscription clock drive completion but punish slow, part-time learners whose access can expire first.
poles: hard time box for completion pressure
pause/extend so slow learners are not punished
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep the completion-tied guarantee but add pause/extend and never erase progress on lapsed access

conflict_axes.name: difficulty_memory_vs_ease_hell
conflict_axes.description: A per-card difficulty state must reflect real hardness without ratcheting into a punitive, hard-to-recover floor.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: adopt a mean-reverting difficulty so a bad week cannot permanently inflate a card's workload

conflict_axes.name: copy_for_popularity_vs_copy_for_function
conflict_axes.description: A popular brand mechanic invites copying by reputation rather than by evidenced function and fit to our system.
poles: copy because a brand is popular
copy for evidenced function with a stated modification
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: extract each mechanism by function/exemplar/what-to-copy/evidence and only adopt with a stated modification and tag

conflict_axes.name: verified_fact_vs_convenient_vendor_number
conflict_axes.description: Portal-gated prices and vendor pass-rate claims tempt asserting a convenient number as fact against the honesty discipline.
poles: assert the convenient vendor number as fact
carry it as a labeled vendor claim / ESTIMATE / UNKNOWN
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: tag every price and pass rate FACT/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN, mark vendor claims as such, and never assert an unverified number

edge_cases.description: INBDE Bootcamp's '99% of target-meeting students pass' is repeated as an established outcome rather than a vendor claim
edge_cases.trigger: a vendor marketing statistic is lifted into a design decision as fact
edge_cases.mitigation: carry the pass rate explicitly as an unverified vendor claim and never let it justify a design verdict

edge_cases.description: A portal-gated price (ETS TestReady itemized prices, SuperMemo 19 current price) is filled in with a guessed number
edge_cases.trigger: an UNKNOWN price is treated as knowable and invented for completeness
edge_cases.mitigation: leave the price UNKNOWN with the gated-portal reason and re-check only when direct access is obtained

edge_cases.description: The streak is implemented to increment on app-open rather than on completed due reviews
edge_cases.trigger: the streak-with-slack copy is shipped without the retrieval binding
edge_cases.mitigation: bind the streak to completed due reviews and retention outcomes, never to app-opens or raw XP

edge_cases.description: The raw 1-5 confidence tap is wired directly to scheduling with no recall calibration
edge_cases.trigger: the confidence-rating copy is adopted without the model-calibration modification
edge_cases.mitigation: feed confidence into a recall-calibrated memory model as one input feature and let the model own scheduling

edge_cases.description: Items 'mastered' in a within-session adaptive round never enter the long-term spaced queue
edge_cases.trigger: session mastery is treated as an exit condition when copying Quizlet-Learn adaptivity
edge_cases.mitigation: route every session-mastered item into the calendar-spaced FSRS queue as a milestone, not an exit

edge_cases.description: A monetization proposal gates spaced review or active recall behind the paywall
edge_cases.trigger: the funnel/guarantee copy is extended to paywall the active-recall core
edge_cases.mitigation: keep the active-recall spaced-review core free/cheap and monetize content depth, feedback and analytics only

edge_cases.description: The placement diagnostic becomes a long mandatory setup before the learner can do a single review
edge_cases.trigger: the diagnostic-seeds-a-plan copy grows into an onboarding cliff
edge_cases.mitigation: keep correct defaults out of the box and require zero mandatory configuration before the first review

edge_cases.description: A slow, part-time foreign-trained dentist loses access to a time-boxed subscription before finishing
edge_cases.trigger: a completion-tied guarantee is combined with a hard subscription clock
edge_cases.mitigation: provide pause/extend options and guarantee progress is not erased on lapsed access

edge_cases.description: Accepted user-generated content is silently removed or an unvetted shared-deck marketplace ships with no quality signal
edge_cases.trigger: content supply is treated as an afterthought behind the scheduler
edge_cases.mitigation: treat user content as a versioned, exportable commitment and attach provenance/accuracy signals to shared decks

edge_cases.description: A board-prep card packs a full topic summary onto one card and a lapse cannot localize the forgotten fact
edge_cases.trigger: wall-of-text authoring is allowed without an atomicity lint
edge_cases.mitigation: enforce atomic cards at authoring time and lint card length so a lapse points to one fact

edge_cases.description: A legacy SM-2 ease-factor scheduler is chosen and cards pin at the 130% ease floor
edge_cases.trigger: the model-based-SR adopt verdict is bypassed for an SM-2 scheduler
edge_cases.mitigation: adopt an FSRS-class mean-reverting difficulty so a bad week cannot permanently inflate workload

edge_cases.description: Our own metrics show engagement rising while retention stalls, but no verdict is re-opened
edge_cases.trigger: a fault the ledger warned about materializes and the loop does not re-run
edge_cases.mitigation: treat an own-metric fault signal as a re-run trigger that re-opens the relevant adopt/adapt/reject verdict

workflow.action: Charter the competitor scan as a recurring benchmark loop
workflow.description: State the loop is periodic, name its mechanism-table and fault-table outputs, and route them to the design backlog not a commercial comparison
workflow.gate: the charter defines a recurring loop with two named outputs feeding the adopt/adapt/reject ledger

workflow.description: State the WebFetch-blocked/WebSearch-verified caveat, the labeling rules, the no-invented-numbers rule and the vendor-claim marking
workflow.gate: every claim carries a tag, vendor claims are marked, and no user count/revenue/pass rate is asserted as fact

workflow.description: List the SR apps, the gamification reference and the exam-prep verticals with feature existence FACT and prices ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN
workflow.gate: each competitor is named with its evidence tags and exemplar attribution preserved

workflow.description: Apply the mechanism/exemplar/what-to-copy/evidence method to produce the copy rows
workflow.gate: each mechanism has a function, an exemplar, a specific what-to-copy with modification, and an evidence tag

workflow.action: Deep-model the model-based-SR and streak-with-slack copies
workflow.description: Detail the FSRS DSR adopt-as-is baseline and the streak-with-slack adapt copy
workflow.gate: the DSR memory state, desired-retention dial and mean-reverting difficulty are stated, and the streak is bound to due-reviews-completed

workflow.action: Deep-model the confidence, adaptive-difficulty, placement and funnel copies
workflow.description: Detail the confidence-as-input, session-adaptivity, placement-diagnostic and funnel/guarantee copies with their modifications
workflow.gate: each copy names its exemplar, evidence tag and the binding modification from its paired fault

workflow.action: Extract the faults to avoid into design rules
workflow.description: Apply the fault/where-documented/design-rule method to produce enforceable rules
workflow.gate: each fault has a documented source with an evidence tag and an enforceable design rule

workflow.description: Detail gamification-over-learning, ease hell, wall-of-text, paywall, content-supply, onboarding-cliff, raw-self-rating, session-mastery and time-boxed faults
workflow.gate: each fault states its evidence, its harm and the design rule and modification it imposes

workflow.description: Record a verdict with rationale, modification and evidence tag per mechanism and fault, and route each to the design backlog
workflow.gate: every mechanism and fault has a tagged verdict with its modification, and no verdict rests on an unlabeled or invented fact

workflow.description: Define the scheduled and event-driven triggers, including the own-metric-fault-surfacing trigger, that refresh the ledger
workflow.gate: the cadence names the triggers and requires each re-run to update the ledger under the honesty discipline

dominance_rules.rule: The honesty discipline dominates any competitor number or verdict
dominance_rules.rationale: WebFetch was blocked and many prices/pass rates are third-party or vendor claims, so an unlabeled number must never drive a decision
dominance_rules.trigger: a price, pass rate, or user count is stated or a verdict is drafted
dominance_rules.action: tag it FACT/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN, mark vendor claims as such, and block any verdict resting on an unlabeled or invented fact

dominance_rules.rule: Learning outcome dominates engagement in any gamification call
dominance_rules.rationale: the streak/league mechanics optimize daily return but certify showing up, not knowing
dominance_rules.action: bind it to completed due reviews and retention outcomes and forbid raw time/XP as a knowledge proxy

dominance_rules.rule: A recall-calibrated model dominates raw self-rating for scheduling
dominance_rules.rationale: confidence is subjective, gameable and coarser than a forgetting curve; confidence != competence
dominance_rules.trigger: a self-rating is used to schedule
dominance_rules.action: use confidence as one calibrated input feature and let a forgetting-curve model own the scheduling decision

dominance_rules.rationale: session mastery decays between sessions without a calendar-spaced follow-up
dominance_rules.trigger: an item is marked mastered in a session
dominance_rules.action: route it into the long-term FSRS queue as a milestone, never treat session mastery as the exit condition

dominance_rules.rule: The active-recall core dominates the monetization surface
dominance_rules.rationale: paywalling the effective features is the Quizlet-2022 trust-destroying fault
dominance_rules.trigger: a monetization proposal touches spaced review or active recall
dominance_rules.action: keep the active-recall core free/cheap and monetize content depth, feedback and analytics instead

dominance_rules.rule: Correct out-of-the-box defaults dominate early personalization
dominance_rules.rationale: the expert-tool onboarding cliff (SuperMemo/Anki/RemNote) kills adoption before the first review
dominance_rules.trigger: a diagnostic or configuration step is placed before the first review
dominance_rules.action: require zero mandatory configuration before the first review and reach a real review in seconds

dominance_rules.rule: Mean-reverting difficulty dominates a ratcheting ease factor
dominance_rules.rationale: SM-2 ease hell permanently inflates workload after a bad run
dominance_rules.trigger: a per-card difficulty scheme is chosen
dominance_rules.action: adopt an FSRS-class mean-reverting difficulty so a bad week cannot pin a card at a punitive floor

dominance_rules.rule: Evidenced function dominates brand popularity in a copy decision
dominance_rules.rationale: copying by reputation imports context that may not fit our system
dominance_rules.trigger: a mechanism is proposed for copying because a brand is popular
dominance_rules.action: require the function/exemplar/what-to-copy/evidence extraction and a stated modification before adopting

dominance_rules.rule: A durable content commitment dominates a convenient content removal
dominance_rules.rationale: removing or abandoning community content (Memrise, Quizlet Gravity) is read as trust-destroying
dominance_rules.trigger: removal or archival of accepted user content is proposed
dominance_rules.action: version and export user content, never silently remove it, and score shared decks with provenance/accuracy signals

anti_rework_rules.rule: Tag every competitor claim FACT/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN and mark vendor claims when the claim is first recorded
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an unverified price or vendor pass-rate claim propagating into a design verdict and being retracted later

anti_rework_rules.rule: Attach each mechanism's binding modification (from its paired fault) at extraction time
anti_rework_rules.prevents: adopting a mechanism raw and re-discovering the fault (streak-as-app-open, raw self-rating, session-only mastery) after implementation

anti_rework_rules.rule: Bind the streak to completed due reviews before building any streak UI
anti_rework_rules.prevents: shipping an app-open streak that rewards attendance and having to re-anchor it to retrieval later

anti_rework_rules.rule: Route session-mastered items into the long-term spaced queue in the first design of the session loop
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a between-session decay problem discovered after learners forget cram-mastered sets

anti_rework_rules.rule: Keep the active-recall core free in the first monetization design
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a Quizlet-2022-style paywall of the effective features that must later be walked back under backlash

anti_rework_rules.rule: Enforce atomic-card authoring and a length lint before content is authored at scale
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a corpus of wall-of-text cards that must be re-split and re-scheduled

anti_rework_rules.rule: Design correct out-of-the-box defaults with zero pre-review configuration from the start
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an onboarding cliff that has to be dismantled after early-learner drop-off

anti_rework_rules.rule: Record each fault-to-avoid as an enforceable design rule the moment it is documented
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a known competitor failure recurring in our system because it was noted but never turned into a rule

anti_rework_rules.rule: Give every mechanism and fault an adopt/adapt/reject verdict on the design backlog before the scan is closed
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an inert feature list that produces no design action and forces a re-scan to recover the decisions

iteration_protocol.trigger: a competitor changes a flagship feature or price (e.g. a new paywall move, a new tier, a removed feature)
iteration_protocol.action: re-verify the roster snapshot, re-tag the affected claim, and update any mechanism/fault verdict that relied on it

iteration_protocol.trigger: one of our own system's feedback metrics surfaces a fault the ledger warned about (e.g. engagement up while retention stalls)
iteration_protocol.action: re-open the relevant fault verdict and re-run its extraction, treating the metric as the loop-that-improves-the-loop signal

iteration_protocol.trigger: a previously UNKNOWN price or a gated vendor page becomes directly fetchable
iteration_protocol.action: replace the UNKNOWN/ESTIMATE with a verified value and re-tag it, then re-check any verdict that referenced it

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new competitor enters the SR/study-app or exam-prep field
iteration_protocol.action: add it to the roster, run the mechanism and fault extraction over it, and add any resulting verdicts to the ledger

iteration_protocol.trigger: a mechanism's binding modification proves insufficient in our own implementation (e.g. calibrated confidence still miscalibrates)
iteration_protocol.action: revise the modification and the mechanism's adapt verdict and re-derive its acceptance test

iteration_protocol.trigger: a fault's evidence is upgraded (a suspected weakness gains a citation) or downgraded
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the fault extraction for it, update its evidence tag and design rule, and refresh its ledger verdict

iteration_protocol.trigger: the scheduled re-scan interval proves mismatched to the design backlog's pace
iteration_protocol.action: retune the benchmark revisit cadence so the ledger stays current without churning faster than the backlog can act

priority_rationale: The benchmark-loop charter, honesty discipline and competitor roster come first because every mechanism and fault decision depends on a defined loop, a labeling contract, and a cited source set; the mechanism-extraction and fault-extraction methods next, because they are the two disciplines that turn the roster into copy rows and design rules; the individual mechanism copies and fault rules then apply those methods to each competitor feature, each mechanism carrying the binding modification from its paired fault; and the adopt/adapt/reject ledger and the revisit cadence come last because they compose every mechanism and fault into tagged, actionable verdicts and keep those verdicts refreshed as the competitor field and our own metrics change.
